mutations.after: delete from usage where org_id = $1 and false
mutations.because: without the usage delete the org row's delete hits the FK constraint and the transaction rolls back; the org survives and the run reports failed instead of expired. The test asserts the org row is gone and usage is 0; under this mutant expect(orgCount[0]!.n).toBe(0) fails on that assertion line.
command: expireOrgTombstones deletes usage then the org row of a purged org older than thirteen months

mutations.after: delete from org where id = $1 and false
mutations.because: without the org row delete the org row survives and the org delete is a no-op. The test asserts the org row count is 0; under this mutant expect(orgCount[0]!.n).toBe(0) fails on that assertion line.

mutations.after: delete from usage where $1::text is not null
mutations.because: the filter is removed so the delete matches every org's usage, not just the named one. The test snapshots beta before and after and asserts equality; under this mutant beta's usage changes, so expect(await snapshot(db, "beta")).toEqual(beforeBeta) fails on that assertion line.
command: expireOrgTombstones deletes usage then the org row of a purged org older than thirteen months

mutations.because: the retention period shrinks to one month, so a tombstone backdated to 12 months is now eligible and gets expired. The younger-tombstone test asserts eligible is empty and the snapshot is unchanged; under this mutant expireOrgTombstones({ apply: true }) deletes the org, so expect(result).toEqual({ eligible: [], ... }) fails on that assertion line.
command: expireOrgTombstones keeps a tombstone younger than thirteen months and its usage

mutations.because: the purged_at guard is removed, so an org with a deletion row that was requested but never purged is eligible. The incomplete-purge test asserts eligible is empty and the snapshot is unchanged; under this mutant the org is listed as eligible and expired, so expect(result).toEqual({ eligible: [], ... }) fails on that assertion line.
command: expireOrgTombstones keeps an old tombstone whose purge is not complete

mutations.because: the local org exclusion is weakened to a tautology, so a backdated-and-purged 'local' org row is eligible for deletion. The local-exclusion test asserts eligible is empty and the local org row still exists; under this mutant local is eligible and deleted, so expect(result).toEqual({ eligible: [], ... }) fails on that assertion line.
command: expireOrgTombstones never expires the local org

mutations.because: the dry-run guard is removed, so a dry run (--apply absent) deletes org tombstones. The dry-run test asserts the org and usage rows are unchanged after a dry run; under this mutant they are deleted, so expect(await snapshot(db, "acme")).toEqual(beforeAcme) fails on that assertion line.
command: org-expire CLI dry run lists eligible orgs and deletes nothing

mutations.because: the switch-off branch is removed, so a setup failure with PURGE_RECONCILE=off counts two failed steps and logs 'reconcile failed' instead of the skip message. The switch-off test asserts failed is 1 and the log contains 'Reconcile skipped: PURGE_RECONCILE=off.'; under this mutant expect(failed).toBe(1) fails on that assertion line.
command: housekeeping with PURGE_RECONCILE=off counts a setup failure as one step and logs the skip
